content:
Rumors suggest this year's Apple fall iPhone lineup will revolve around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are three of the biggest feature differences (excluding price) that could influence your decision on whether to upgrade.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but worth highlighting specifically because it is also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic iPhone design that has been used for years. Their display sizes and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you prefer the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top pick.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. Its design is completely different — the outer display is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner display is similar to an iPad mini.

Cameras: Pro remains the best choice

Apple has always packed its most advanced and innovative camera technology into the Pro models. This year will be no different.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature mostly the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not include a telephoto lens.

Reports indicate that the iPhone Ultra will still have the same main, ultrawide, and front cameras as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro series, and is rumored to be further enhanced this year.

Performance: Same A20 Pro chip, different materials

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to feature the same A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will continue using the same unibody aluminum design as the iPhone 17 Pro, along with a vapor chamber for cooling. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance better than its predecessor, as the iPhone can stay cooler under heavy workloads.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a sleek titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. While it may also feature a vapor chamber, only one leaker has mentioned it so far. Even so, due to the different materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may still perform slightly worse under direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
